newsitem.title: INDIA: Five killed in India gunbattle with separatists.
newsitem.headline: Five killed in India gunbattle with separatists.

text.p: Three separatist guerrillas and two soldiers were killed in a gunbattle in the northeastern Indian state of Assam, police said on Sunday.
They said the gunbattle took place on Saturday night in the tea and oil-rich district of Tinsukia, 300 km (180 miles) east of Guwahati, the state's main city.
The separatists, who are seeking an autonomous Assamese homeland, attacked an army patrol, killing two soldiers and injuring six. The soldiers retaliated, killing three separatists, police said.
Assamese guerrillas accuse India's federal government of exploiting the state's rich mineral and timber resources and giving little in return.
Indian officials have said they believe the movement has been largely contained.

Saturday's incident was the first since India's federal government unified police, paramilitary troops and the army under a single commander last month to help combat separatism and insurgency in the state.

The state also has witnessed violent incidents involving Bodo tribals seeking a homeland carved out of Assam. Bodo separatists claimed responsibility for a bomb attack on a train in December that killed at least 34 people in the northern part of the state.
